title: Sales Data Reconciliation
description: Compares CSR-tracked data (Office Tracking CSV) with ServSuite system data to surface discrepancies and ensure accurate reporting.

discrepancies.explanation: ServSuite shows 14 more sales than CSR tracking. CSRs may miss logging some sales, or ServSuite counts program upgrades as new sales.

ServSuite records ALL cancel events (441 events, 134 unique accounts) including auto-cancels, program changes, etc. CSRs only log cancels they process directly (143). These are fundamentally different counts.
Revenue is only tracked in ServSuite via invoices. $778,248 from 8,042 invoices. The Office Tracking CSV does not capture revenue amounts.

cancelReasonComparison.note: CSV uses simplified categories (Paused/WP, Moved, etc.). ServSuite has granular reasons. Direct comparison is approximate.

salesComparison.note: CSV tracks sale type (Standard, Misting System, etc.). ServSuite tracks both program and lead source independently.

insights.title: CSR tracking misses sales
insights.detail: 14 sales (7%) in ServSuite are not reflected in CSR tracking. This means the daily sales count Yoel sees is underreported. Possible causes: techs closing sales in the field (not logged by CSRs), online self-service activations, or program upgrades counted as new sales in ServSuite.
insights.action: Audit the sales gap — pull ServSuite new customer list and cross-reference with CSR log to find the missing entries.

insights.title: Tech upsells severely underreported
insights.detail: Only 6 tech upsells logged in the CSV. With 91 total sales and techs in the field daily, this is almost certainly incomplete. Upsell attribution helps measure tech sales performance and incentives.
insights.action: Implement a simple upsell logging workflow — tech texts CSR with customer name, CSR logs it. Or build a simple form in GHL.

insights.title: Revenue tracking gap
insights.detail: YTD revenue is $778,248 across 8,042 invoices (avg $97/invoice). The Office Tracking CSV doesn't include revenue amounts, so the sales dashboard can't show dollar values per sale or per CSR.
insights.action: Add a "Sale Value" column to the Office Tracking sheet, or better yet, pull revenue data directly from ServSuite into the dashboard.

insights.title: Recoverable cancel opportunity
insights.detail: 121 cancel events (27%) are flagged as recoverable in ServSuite. These are customers who paused or expressed temporary disinterest — prime targets for reactivation as peak season starts.
insights.action: Build a reactivation campaign list from recoverable cancels. Target with seasonal restart offer via GHL automation.

methodology.csvTracking: CSRs manually enter each sale and cancel event in the Office Tracking Excel sheet. Power Automate exports this to CSV daily.
methodology.servSuiteTracking: ServSuite records all account activations, work orders, invoices, and cancel events automatically. Data is exported nightly via Playwright automation.
keyDifferences: CSV counts CSR-entered events; ServSuite counts system events
CSV cancel categories are simplified (6-8 buckets); ServSuite has 15+ specific reasons
ServSuite includes revenue data; CSV does not
ServSuite counts ALL cancel events including program changes; CSV only counts customer-initiated cancels
CSV includes tech upsell attribution; ServSuite does not easily surface this
